inspiration: Zone ambience as emitters: each source has a radius and a fade-out time; fade-in is half of that, capped at 5 s (zone_sound_emitter.cpp 160-166). Recreate the fade rule with our own sound beds.
Day and night variants of one ambience swap with a short crossfade (2 s constant in zone_audio_manager.cpp line 137) rather than a hard cut.

Music follows position, not zone: the music track is the closest music region that contains the listener (zone_audio_manager.cpp 247-268). One zone can hold several music beds, so a biome change is a region change.

Weather as a timed state machine: a check interval, a per-weather duration, 10 s transitions, and a rain chance summed over four slots out of a 400 roll, then split into storm, rain and light rain (weather_system.cpp 19-47, 168-238). The timer and blend logic is the transferable part; the particles are not.

Cast effects pick a visual preset by spell style: a spray cone for some casts, a glow for others. Colour comes from the spell and the particle lifetime is set to the cast time (spell_visual_fx.cpp 327-345). Our spell colour rule can reuse this shape.
Rain as a spell: a radius-scaled rain volume lasts exactly the spell duration (spell_visual_fx.cpp 633-650). Area-of-effect weather from a caster is a clear, cheap read at 375 wide.

Zone connections as data: each zone-line record has a trigger point, a landing rule and a target zone, kept as one JSON file per zone (data/zone_lines/*.json). This matches our rule that zones are data on one runtime.
Item to model lookup as a plain id-to-number table loaded from data (data/item_models.json), not hard-coded in the renderer. Simple and easy to audit.

briefs.label: Cast-spray cone
briefs.why: A caster's school colour spreads outward in a cone or a steady glow, so the spell reads at a glance during a fight.
briefs.keep: colour taken from the spell; a spray style for some casts and a glow style for others; effect lifetime set to the cast time
briefs.change: a different cone shape and sprite; a gold and smoke palette instead of the donor's colour ramp; a short ring burst at the end instead of a fade

briefs.label: Rolling storm front
briefs.why: Weather that changes on a timer and blends in over ten seconds gives a fight arena a sense of time passing.
briefs.keep: check interval plus per-weather duration; 10 s blend between states; a storm that lasts a set minute range
briefs.change: the effect is fog thickening and light dimming, not rain particles; the storm also changes enemy aggro radius visibly; a single forecast cue on the HUD

briefs.label: Zone-line rift
briefs.why: A portal is a trigger volume plus a landing point; the data is clear and the player knows where they will arrive.
briefs.keep: trigger point and landing rule held in one per-zone data file; a target zone field
briefs.change: a torn ground seam with a low hum instead of a door; the landing is shown as a ring on the ground; no coordinates copied

briefs.label: Dual-state ambience bed
briefs.why: One ambience loop with a day and a night version, swapped with a crossfade, gives a zone two moods for little asset cost.
briefs.keep: two variants of one loop; crossfade on switch; the variant chosen by a single world flag
briefs.change: switch on combat state (idle versus engaged) rather than time of day; a third variant for low health; our own sound design

briefs.label: Nearest music region
briefs.why: Overlapping music regions are resolved by the nearest one, so walking between beds feels natural.
briefs.keep: a region is a point plus radius; the nearest containing region wins
briefs.change: blend the two music beds by weight instead of a hard switch; resolve overlaps by fight state, not by distance
